soft_issues: The authors list spatial planning among keywords. The analysis is still a lice-network simulation, not a coastal-plan or licence study.

claim_checks.claim: This is a stochastic lice simulation in PA3, not a coastal-plan or licensing study. PA3 is 3646 km2 with 147 active farms in 2014-2017. Average standing stock 544 000 fish.
claim_checks.extract_quote: PA3 covers an area of 3646 km2, and includes 147 farms that were actively producing salmonids during the study period (January 2014–December 2017).
claim_checks.note: The paper's keywords include spatial planning. The object remains lice on historic production.

claim_checks.claim: The lice model is Aldrin et al. 2019. Biomass from closed farms is moved to matching cohorts. Nine scenarios: baseline, random 20-50 percent, strategic 20-50 percent. 45 000 simulations.
claim_checks.extract_quote: The results from all 45 000 simulations are summarized as yearly averages for each of the 9 scenarios
claim_checks.note: The downward-trend parameter from Aldrin 2019 was set to zero.

claim_checks.claim: Closing farms reduced simulated adult-female lice by 4-15 percent, other motiles by 6-23 percent, and treatments by 6-25 percent. Strategic 50 percent: median 15, 23 and 25 percent.
claim_checks.extract_quote: the average number of AF and OM sal mon lice was reduced by 4–15 and 6–23%, respectively
claim_checks.note: Scenario 9 medians are stated in the results section.

claim_checks.claim: Random-removal treatments fell by 6-17 percent. Strategic-removal treatments fell by 14-25 percent. Strategic removal outperformed random removal.
claim_checks.extract_quote: the average fish experience between 6 and 17% less treatments in the random removal scenarios, and between 14 and 25% less treatments in the strategic removal scenarios.
claim_checks.note: The authors treat this as network fragmentation, not a siting recipe.

claim_checks.claim: Some farms exceed 5 million fish, maximum 18.2 million, outside the fitted range. Methods are not a procedure to optimise farm structure in PA3.
claim_checks.extract_quote: the farms grew to become unrealistically large, with a few farms in the most radical scenarios exceeding 5 million fish, and a maximum of 18.2 million fish
claim_checks.note: Four numbered caveats are in the discussion.

evidence_direction_note: supports_effect is defensible for the paper's own claim that redistributing the same biomass onto fewer, more distant farms reduces simulated lice and treatments.
priority_questions_note: A5 only (density, farm structure, lice). A3 not tagged. Trade-offs here are lice versus network structure, not coastal coexistence.
coi_note: Funding is RCN 254830/E40 plus NVI and IMR. No competing-interest statement. coi_declared remains unclear.
extract_coverage: Walked the full extracted.md: title and abstract, introduction (national host density), methods (PA3, Aldrin 2019, nine scenarios), results, discussion caveats, acknowledgements, and references.
